acceptance: FileContainsAny, CountOccurrencesAny and LineContainsAll each have a form that, on a missing path, fails with a message naming the path and the moved-file possibility; an error result still satisfies errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist).
An existing path that simply lacks the content fails without the moved-file hint.
Unit tests in go/pkg/acsassert/assertions_test.go cover the missing-path and existing-path cases for each reader.
fix: Add a message-carrying form of each reader, either a TB-taking variant or a (value, error) variant whose not-exist error carries the same moved-file hint as FileContains, and migrate callers or document when the lenient form remains correct.
notes: Split out of acs-cycle50-predicates-point-at-a-moved-file (cycle 1702): the value-only signatures cannot carry a message without an API change, so that cycle covered the message-carrying readers only.
problem: Cycle 1702 made every acsassert reader that can report a failure (a TB parameter or an error result) name the moved-file possibility on a not-exist read. FileContainsAny, CountOccurrencesAny and LineContainsAll return only a bool or int, so on a missing path they return false or 0 and the calling predicate fails with its own content message, which says nothing about a missing or moved file. 46 predicate files under go/acs call at least one of them.
title: acsassert's value-only readers (FileContainsAny, CountOccurrencesAny, LineContainsAll) swallow a missing path, so a moved file fails their predicates without the moved-file hint
